picks.title: Scientists who use AI propose less distinctive ideas for federal research grants
picks.rationale: Metascience result on how science itself is changing: AI-assisted U.S. federal grant proposals cluster closer to already-funded topics, and at NIH AI-heavy proposals won more often but preceded more routine papers.
picks.excerpt: A new study of U.S. federal grant applications suggests that scientists using generative AI tend to pitch research closer to previously funded topics. At the NIH, AI-heavy proposals won funding more often and preceded modestly more routine papers.

picks.title: From 400 miles above Earth, AI tracks invasive leafy spurge
picks.rationale: University of Minnesota combines satellite imagery, deep learning and community-science data to map 20 years of invasive leafy spurge spread — AI as an ecology field method.
picks.excerpt: Harnessing satellite imagery, AI deep-learning models and community science data, scientists from the University of Minnesota have tracked the spread of leafy spurge over a 20-year period.

picks.title: Less data, faster discovery: Researchers rethink AI's role in developing new materials
picks.rationale: Challenges the 'train on millions of simulations' approach to electronic-structure prediction, showing materials-discovery models can work with far less data — a method shift for computational materials science.
picks.excerpt: Developing new materials often starts with understanding their electronic structure, or how electrons are arranged and behave within them. Calculating these electronic structures typically requires expensive simulations on supercomputers. That's led researchers to train artificial intelligence models on millions of simulated data points to make faster predictions.

picks.title: Quantum neural networks with high-dimensional quantum neurons
picks.rationale: National Science Review paper scales a quantum neural network with backpropagation on a qudit processor — high-dimensional neurons instead of more qubits, a new route for quantum ML hardware.
picks.excerpt: How can we scale up a quantum neural network? One way is to add more qubits as neurons. But a study titled "Quantum neural network equipped with backpropagation on a qudit processor" published in National Science Review shows another way.

picks.title: Scientists might have discovered what makes AI so effective at chess
picks.rationale: Cognitive-science angle on game AI: research suggests chess engines' edge comes from comfort with complex positions humans avoid — insight into machine versus human cognition.
picks.excerpt: AI's comfort with complexity could be key to its chess-playing prowess

Cross-section: the picks' domains (phys.org, techxplore.com, psypost.org, scientificamerican.com) do not appear in the medicine block of published_urls.json, and no 11-17 cross-section assignment touches science. Not picked on judgement: Phys.org plastic pyrolysis impurities (good, but kept Phys.org to 1 and materials to 1 — Tech Xplore less-data item is the broader method story); SciAm 'young mathematicians' survey (kept SciAm to 1, overlaps the metascience lane of the PsyPost grant study); Phys.org Euclid lenses (AI incidental, ML only a first filter); Tech Xplore CLARA bioreactor (published 11-11, older, Tech Xplore already at 2); Medical Xpress SfN neuroscience roundup (conference preview, no single result). Outlets: 4 distinct (Tech Xplore x2, others x1); topics: metascience, ecology/remote sensing, materials, quantum, cognition.
